text:
alex: Heads-up: saw ~800 requests routed to v1 in last 10m despite clients sending `X-Client-Version: 2`. Console shows affinity pinned to v1 for the token.

maria: hmm. Any pattern on token vs route? Did the header arrive at edge or get dropped?

alex: sample from edge logs:
```
GET /v1/generate
X-Client-Version: 2
Authorization: Bearer tok_abc
```
Edge -> ingress shows header, but our proxy removes `X-Client-Version` before hitting routing service.

sam: that's the proxy sanitizer we added for auth headers. It shouldn't strip version headers though. I can reproduce locally with dev-proxy.

irene: Is the pin TTL long? We recently bumped pin TTL to 12h for stability.

tasha: It's 12h currently for tokens created before the rollout. New tokens get 5m.

maria: We need two things: (1) fix proxy not to strip the header; (2) backfill routing metrics so console can surface "version mismatch" badge for affected tenants.

alex: Agreed. Also quota attribution currently counts against v1 which inflates v1 token usage. That will affect reserved capacity sliding windows.

sam: quick patch: stop stripping `X-Client-Version` in proxy and add a log label `client_version` to routing traces. I'll cut a canary.

deploy-bot: deploy started for sam/proxy-fix -> staging (sha: a1b2c3) :rocket: 

irene: After canary, let's run a small cohort (5 tenants) through new path and check console diff for per-route quota meters.

tasha: I'll add a console flag to show "sticky pin TTL" and expose a histogram for pin-age so PMs can see how many tokens are long-pinned.

maria: Also add a one-off alert: if >100 v1-routed requests with `X-Client-Version: 2` per minute, create a ticket automatically.

alex: thanks. Filing follow-up: #12345 - routing header preservation + attribution.
